title: Die Siedler
statementMd:
## Problem Statement

Snuke is playing a game using $n$ kinds of cards called Card $1$ through Card $n$. There are $m$ kinds of card packs available in this game; the $i$-th pack contains $s_{i,j}$ copies of Card $j$. Every pack contains at least one card.

Initially, Snuke has $c_j$ copies of Card $j$ (it is guaranteed that he has at least one card in total).

He can do the following operations any number of times in any order:

- Get a card pack: Choose $i=1$, $\dots$, or $m$ and get all cards contained in the $i$-th pack.
- Exchange cards: Choose $j=1$, $\dots$, or $n$, discard $2j$ copies of Card $j$, and get one copy of Card $((j \text{ mod } n) + 1)$. (He must have at least $2j$ copies of Card $j$.)

Snuke wants to have as few cards as possible in total. Find the minimum number of cards that Snuke can end up with.

## Constraints

- $2 \le n \le 16$
- $1 \le m \le 50$
- $0 \le s_{i,j}, c_j \lt 2j$
- $c_1+\dots +c_n>0$
- $s_{i,1}+\dots +s_{i,n}>0$

## Input

Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:

```
n m
c_1 \dots c_n
s_{1,1} \dots s_{1,n}
\vdots
s_{m,1} \dots s_{m,n}
```

## Output

Print the minimum number of cards that Snuke can end up with.
statementZhMd:
## 题目描述

Snuke 正在玩一个使用 $n$ 种卡片的游戏，这些卡片被称为卡片 1 至卡片 $n$。游戏中有 $m$ 种卡包可供选择；第 $i$ 种卡包中包含 $s_{i,j}$ 张卡片 $j$。每种卡包中至少包含一张卡片。

初始时，Snuke 拥有 $c_j$ 张卡片 $j$（保证他总共至少拥有一张卡片）。

他可以以任意顺序进行任意多次以下操作：

- 获取卡包：选择 $i=1$、$\dots$ 或 $m$，获取第 $i$ 种卡包中包含的全部卡片。
- 交换卡片：选择 $j=1$、$\dots$ 或 $n$，丢弃 $2j$ 张卡片 $j$，并获得一张卡片 $((j \text{ mod } n) + 1)$。（他必须至少拥有 $2j$ 张卡片 $j$。）

Snuke 希望最终拥有的卡片总数尽可能少。请找出 Snuke 最终能够拥有的卡片总数的最小值。

## 约束条件

- $2 \le n \le 16$
- $1 \le m \le 50$
- $0 \le s_{i,j}, c_j \lt 2j$
- $c_1+\dots +c_n>0$
- $s_{i,1}+\dots +s_{i,n}>0$

## 输入格式

输入从标准输入按以下格式给出：

```
n m
c_1 \dots c_n
s_{1,1} \dots s_{1,n}
\vdots
s_{m,1} \dots s_{m,n}
```

## 输出格式

输出 Snuke 最终能够拥有的卡片总数的最小值。

samples.note: By getting two packs of the second kind and one pack of the first kind, and then exchanging cards some number of times, Snuke can end up with one copy of Card $4$ and one copy of Card $5$.
